01 / CAPABILITIES

What can your AI do in Moodle?

From a first course draft to daily administration, MoodlIA gives an AI assistant a broad but permission-controlled set of Moodle capabilities.

01

Build courses

Create categories, courses, sections, activities, Books, Pages, and complete learning structures.

“Create a six-week onboarding course.”
02

Create content

Write polished learning material, organise chapters, attach files, and add portable interactive demonstrations.

“Turn this document into an interactive Book.”
03

Manage people

Create users, enrol learners, assign roles, and organise groups, cohorts, and groupings.

“Enrol the sales team in the new course.”
04

Assess learning

Prepare assignments, question banks, quizzes, rubrics, grades, feedback, and completion rules.

“Build a ten-question knowledge check.”
05

Monitor progress

Inspect participation, grades, completion, course readiness, and learner progress.

“Who needs help before Friday?”
06

Protect your work

Review changes, audit configuration, create native Moodle backups, and restore courses when needed.

“Check the course and create a backup.”

02 / INSTALL

Install only the parts you need.

The Moodle plugin is the essential bridge. The CLI, Node client, and authoring skills are optional ways to use or extend it.

Required1

Moodle plugin

Install local_moodlia in Moodle, enable its web service, and create a token for a dedicated user.

Get the plugin ↗
Connect2

Your AI assistant

Give your AI client the MoodlIA endpoint and token. It can then discover the available Moodle actions.

Connection guide ↗
Optional3

CLI and Node client

Install the public package when you also want terminal commands, scripts, CI, or a Node application.

npm install -g moodlia
Optional4

Authoring skills

Add the two downloadable skills when you want an AI to design rich Moodle content and operate MoodlIA safely.

View the skills

In everyday use: once connected, you work by asking your AI—not by memorising commands.

03 / ARCHITECTURE

One bridge between AI and Moodle.

MoodlIA does not replace Moodle or keep a second copy of your courses. It translates authorised requests into standard Moodle actions.

AI assistantCommand lineNode application
→
MoodlIAPermission checks · validation · consistent actions
→
MoodleCourses · people · content · assessment · reports
Moodle stays authoritativeNo parallel database.Permissions still applyThe token only does what its user can do.Courses stay portableNative backups restore without MoodlIA.

04 / FUNCTIONALITY

A few things MoodlIA can handle.

The project currently exposes 240 Moodle operations. These examples show the range without turning this page into an API reference.

COURSE CREATION

From a brief to a complete course

Draft the structure, create activities, add content, configure completion, review, and publish.

Brief→Course→Review
RICH CONTENT

Books learners want to explore

Visually polished chapters, local media, diagrams, and self-contained interactive demonstrations that remain portable.

ASSESSMENT

Quizzes, questions, grades, and feedback

Build question banks, configure quizzes, grade work, and inspect results.

PEOPLE

Users, enrolments, roles, and groups

Manage access and organise learners without repetitive administration.

CONTROL

Read first. Change once. Verify.

Inspect content, settings, plugin versions, dependencies, and updates before applying a focused, permission-checked change.

05 / OPTIONAL SKILLS

Two skills extend the authoring experience.

They help the AI design better Moodle learning material and use MoodlIA consistently. Courses do not depend on the skills after publication.
